zh.title: 華航機上雜誌Dynasty獲美國APEX出版獎肯定
zh.summary: 華航機上雜誌Dynasty獲美國APEX雜誌版面設計獎及電子期刊卓越獎。
body: 中華航空股份有限公司機上雜誌Dynasty以光影視覺敘事手法描繪義大利羅馬、越南峴港等目的地魅力，獲美國APEX年度優秀出版獎雜誌版面設計獎項大獎，並摘下電子期刊卓越獎。
華航發布新聞稿指出，美國APEX優秀出版獎由國際出版專業評審團隊評選全球優秀作品，Dynasty以全新升級設計及內容脫穎而出。評審團隊讚賞其優美設計及清晰流暢文字表現，即使涵蓋多語言內容仍井然有序且閱讀友善。
華航表示，Dynasty今年全新改版升級，以更鮮明視覺版面提升閱讀質感，新增時下趨勢單元，精選全球特色建築及當代熱門話題，並擴充節慶專題與美食專欄。

en.title: China Airlines inflight magazine Dynasty wins APEX publishing awards
en.summary: China Airlines' Dynasty magazine wins APEX magazine layout design award and digital periodical excellence award.
body: China Airlines' inflight magazine Dynasty received the magazine layout design grand prize at the U.S. APEX Outstanding Publication Awards and also earned the digital periodical excellence award, according to a press release issued by the airline.

Dynasty uses light-and-shadow visual storytelling to depict destinations such as Rome, Italy and Da Nang, Vietnam. The APEX awards are judged by an international panel of publishing professionals evaluating outstanding works worldwide.

The judging panel particularly praised the magazine's elegant design and clear, fluent writing, noting that despite multilingual content it remains well-organized and reader-friendly, blending practical travel information with artistic aesthetics.

China Airlines said Dynasty was fully revamped this year with sharper visual layouts, adding a trends section featuring distinctive global architecture and contemporary topics, along with expanded festival and food columns.

zh.title: 漢翔實測無人機視覺導航系統 無GPS完成2公里自主飛行
zh.summary: 漢翔實測AIxVNAV視覺導航系統；無GPS條件完成2公里自主飛行
body: 漢翔公司於2026年8月11日攜手合作夥伴Vantor公司，挑戰「2026總統盃無人機競賽」場域。在無GPS訊號的測試條件下，搭載AIxVNAV視覺導航定位系統的無人機，穩定完成約2公里的自主飛行測試任務。
該系統導入美國空間情報公司Vantor調校升級的「Raptor Guide視覺定位技術V1.0」，並由漢翔完成無人機系統整合。系統透過機載相機取得地面影像，並與3D資料庫進行即時比對，協助無人機判斷位置，使其在GPS受干擾或失去訊號時仍可獨立導航。
「2026總統盃無人機競賽」由總統賴清德指示辦理，旨在複雜環境下考驗無人機的高精度定位與AI辨識能力。漢翔作為競賽協助廠商，藉由本次實機飛行驗證系統重現性，持續推動相關技術走向實際應用。

en.title: AIDC Tests AIxVNAV Drone System with 2 km GPS-Denied Flight
en.summary: AIDC tested its AIxVNAV drone visual navigation system in a two-kilometer GPS-denied autonomous flight test.
body: Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) conducted a flight test on August 11, 2026, using its AIxVNAV visual navigation positioning system at the 2026 Presidential Cup Drone Competition arena alongside partner company Vantor. Under GPS-denied testing conditions, the drone completed an autonomous flight mission covering approximately two kilometers.

The AIxVNAV system incorporates Raptor Guide visual positioning technology V1.0, upgraded and tuned by U.S. geospatial intelligence firm Vantor, with full system integration performed by AIDC. The technology uses airborne cameras to capture ground imagery and compares it against a 3D database to determine position, enabling autonomous navigation when GPS signals are denied or unreliable.

The 2026 Presidential Cup Drone Competition was ordered by President Lai Ching-te to test high-precision targeting, autonomous navigation, and AI recognition in complex environments. Serving as an assisting partner, AIDC utilized the arena for flight validation to verify system repeatability and support practical operational deployment.

zh.title: KAI與Hyundai Rotem合作研發KF-21空對空飛彈
zh.summary: 雙方簽署備忘錄共同研發空對空飛彈；首批戰機預計二〇二八年交付
body: 根據AeroTime報導，韓國航太工業（KAI）與Hyundai Rotem於2026年8月12日在南韓泗川的KAI總部簽署合作備忘錄。雙方將共同研發與整合KF-21「獵鷹」（Boramae）戰鬥機的國產遠程空對空飛彈，並計劃合作開拓國內外市場與包裹式出口。
此項研發計畫由南韓國防科學研究所（ADD）主導，預計於2026年至2033年間進行，旨在減少對歐洲「流星」等進口飛彈的依賴。此外，南韓防衛事業廳已於2026年7月29日宣布KF-21開發案正式完成，KAI計劃於2028年前向南韓空軍交付首批40架戰機。

en.title: KAI and Hyundai Rotem Partner to Develop Long-Range Air-to-Air Missiles for KF-21
en.summary: KAI and Hyundai Rotem agreed on August 12 to develop missiles for KF-21 fighters.
body: According to AeroTime, Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI) and Hyundai Rotem signed a memorandum of understanding on August 12, 2026, at KAI's headquarters in Sacheon, South Korea. The agreement covers the joint development and systems integration of long-range air-to-air missiles for the KF-21 Boramae fighter, alongside plans to explore package-type export models and joint marketing opportunities.

The domestic missile development effort is led by South Korea's Agency for Defense Development (ADD) and is scheduled to run from 2026 to 2033. The program aims to reduce the air force's reliance on imported beyond-visual-range missiles. Additionally, the Defense Acquisition Program Administration declared the KF-21 development program complete on July 29, 2026. KAI plans to deliver the first batch of 40 KF-21s to the Republic of Korea Air Force by 2028.
